mainTopic: Salt in the מקדש: מעילה, the כהנים' use of communal salt, and בן בוכרי on the half-shekel
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא: salt already on a limb of a קרבן is subject to מעילה, but salt sitting on the כבש or on top of the מזבח is not. רב מתנה brings a פסוק in יחזקאל as the source. A משנה in שקלים says בית דין let the כהנים benefit from the salt and wood, and שמואל limits this to 'their קרבנות', not eating. The גמרא first reads this as salting their own offerings. It challenges that reading, since salt was given even to cure the hides of קדשים. It then reads שמואל as allowing salt for eating קדשים but not for חולין. רבינא supports the second reading: a ברייתא proves salt comes from communal supplies for every ישראל, so the כהנים would need no special rule just to salt their offerings. רב מרדכי answers in the name of רב שישא that the rule is needed according to בן בוכרי, who holds that כהנים do not have to give the half-shekel. This answer revives the first reading. The גמרא quotes the משנה about בן בוכרי and explains how a כהן who pays hands his coin over to the community. It then begins to explain the mistaken idea the salt rule corrects, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Salt on a limb is subject to misuse, salt on the ramp or altar is not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that salt already placed on a limb of a קרבן carries מעילה. Salt lying on the כבש or on top of the מזבח does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if salt is on the limb of an offering, a person who uses it is guilty of מעילה. If the salt is on the ramp or on top of the altar, he is not guilty of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that draws a line between salt that is already on a limb and salt that is just stored on the כבש or the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt rubbed onto the limb has become part of the קרבן itself, so it takes on the קרבן's holiness and the laws of מעילה. Salt that is only waiting on the כבש or the מזבח has not yet become part of any offering. Using it for oneself is therefore not מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: one is liable for מְעִילָה, the misuse of holy property for personal benefit
a limb or piece of a קרבן being offered on the מזבח
the ramp leading up to the מזבח
the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is saying the salt on the כבש is not holy or not for the מקדש. It only says that using it is not counted as מעילה, because it has not yet become part of a קרבן.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Salt that is on the limb
one is liable for misuse with it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ וְשֶׁבְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: salt that is on the ramp, and salt that is on top of the altar
one is not liable for misuse with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶלַח שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הָאֵבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about salt in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt on a limb of a קרבן is subject to מעילה. Salt on the כבש or on top of the מזבח is not.

steps.title: The verse showing that salt on the limb is part of the offering
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה brings a פסוק in יחזקאל. It calls the limbs together with their salt an עולה, which shows the salt on the limb is part of the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: what is the פסוק for this? 'And you shall offer them before ה׳, and the כהנים shall throw salt on them, and they shall offer them up as an עולה to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה gives the source in the פסוקים for the first half of the ברייתא: salt on the limb carries מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, salt is thrown on the limbs first, and only then are 'they' offered as an עולה. So the salted limb as a whole is called the עולה, and that includes the salt. Because the salt counts as part of the עולה, it gets the law of מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the פסוק that teaches this?
a burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
and they shall throw (cast)

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'and רב מתנה said' (the word in round brackets); the corrected wording in square brackets is just 'רב מתנה said.'

phrases.english: What is the verse?
"And you shall offer them before the Lord,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 43:24

phrases.english: and the priests shall cast salt upon them,
and they shall offer them up as a burnt offering to the Lord."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק behind the ruling in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That salt on the limb carries מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 43:24, which calls the salted limbs an עולה

steps.title: A משנה lets the priests benefit from the salt and the wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in שקלים. Among the rulings of בית דין is that the כהנים may make use of the מקדש's salt and wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: about the salt and about the wood, it was ruled that the כהנים may benefit from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה about the salt in the מקדש. It is setting up a statement of שמואל that explains this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, using things bought for the מקדש would be a problem. This משנה reports a special ruling of בית דין that the כהנים may benefit from the salt and the wood. It fits the first ברייתא, which said that salt not yet on a limb does not carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: benefit from, make use of
the wood used for the fire on the מזבח

phrases.english: We learned there:
About the salt and about the wood,
phrases.notes: This line comes from a list in משנה שקלים of things בית דין made rulings 'about,' which is why it starts that way.

phrases.english: that the priests may benefit from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: עַל הַמֶּלַח וְעַל הָעֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא about מעילה to a related משנה about the כהנים using the salt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים may benefit from the מקדש's salt and wood.

steps.title: שמואל limits the permission to their offerings, not to eating
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's permission covers only use 'for their קרבנות', not use for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the משנה only taught this for their offerings, but for eating, no.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the משנה. The כהנים may use the salt for their offerings, but not for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not explain what 'their קרבנות' and 'eating' mean exactly. That unclear wording is what the גמרא will try to work out in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this in the case of
for their offerings
eating

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
They taught this only for their offerings,
but for eating, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְקׇרְבָּנָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission in the משנה of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים may use the salt only 'for their קרבנות', not for eating.

steps.title: First guess at what שמואל meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes that 'their קרבנות' means salting the כהנים' own offerings. It assumes 'eating' means salting the קדשים meat the כהנים eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: We first thought: what does 'for their offerings' mean? To salt their offerings. And 'to eat' means eating קדשים meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first reading of שמואל's words. It is setting up a challenge against that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this first reading, the כהנים may salt their own קרבנות on the מזבח. But they may not take salt to season the קדשים meat they are given to eat. The phrase קא סלקא דעתין signals that this reading will soon be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: we were assuming; it entered our mind (a first idea that will be challenged)
to salt
eating sacrificial meat

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the גמרא's first assumption, and it is challenged right away in step 6. Do not treat it as settled yet.

phrases.english: It entered our mind:
what is 'for their offerings'?
To salt their offerings.
And 'to eat' means the eating of sacrificial meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to define the terms in שמואל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do 'their קרבנות' and 'eating' mean in שמואל's statement?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First guess: salting their own offerings is allowed, but salting קדשים meat for eating is not.

steps.title: If salt is given even for hides, surely it is given for eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first reading. The כהנים get salt even to cure the hides of קדשים, so it makes no sense to refuse them salt for eating קדשים meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we give the כהנים salt to salt the hides of קדשים, and we would not give them salt for eating קדשים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first reading of שמואל with a logical argument from a lesser use to a greater one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Curing hides is a much weaker use of the salt than seasoning holy meat, which is itself a מצוה. If the weaker use is allowed, the stronger one should be too. So the first reading of שמואל cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: now (introduces an argument that one case is stronger than the other)
hides (skins) of sacrificial animals
we give

phrases.english: Now, to salt the hides of sacrificial animals we give salt,
and for eating sacrificial meat we do not give it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of שמואל proposed in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first reading of שמואל, that salt may not be used for eating קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If salt is given for a lesser use (curing hides), it must be given for a greater use (seasoning holy meat).

steps.title: Proof that salt was used for the hides of sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three places salt was kept in the מקדש. One of them, the לשכת המלח, was for salting the hides of קדשים. This proves the starting point of the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: you find that salt was placed in three places: in the Chamber of Salt, on the ramp, and on top of the altar. In the Chamber of Salt, because there they salted the hides of קדשים. On the ramp, because there they salted the limbs. On top of the altar, because there they salted the קומץ, the לבונה, the קטורת, the מנחת כהנים, the מנחת כהן משיח, the מנחת נסכים, and the עולת העוף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what the challenge assumed: the כהנים were really given salt to cure hides of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first place, the לשכת המלח, was set aside for salting hides, and hides are given to the כהנים for their own benefit. This proves salt was provided even for that lesser use. That gives the challenge in step 6 its force. The other two places line up with the first ברייתא's mention of the כבש and the top of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: you are found to be saying (it turns out that)
the Chamber of Salt in the עזרה
the handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
the flour offering that comes with the wine libations
a bird brought as a burnt offering

steps.whatToRemember: Salt was kept in three places: the לשכת המלח (for hides), the כבש (for limbs), and the top of the מזבח (for מנחות, incense, and bird עולות). The hides proof is what makes the גמרא's challenge to the first reading of שמואל work.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
You are found to be saying,
the salt is placed in three places:
in the Chamber of Salt,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: and on the ramp, and on top of the altar.

phrases.aramaic: בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַמֶּלַח – שֶׁשָּׁם מוֹלְחִין עוֹרוֹת קָדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: In the Chamber of Salt, because there they salt the hides of sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: These hides were given to the כהנים, which is why this counts as using salt for their own benefit.

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ – שֶׁשָּׁם מוֹלְחִים אֶת הָאֵבָרִים,
phrases.english: on the ramp, because there they salt the limbs,
on top of the altar,
because there they salt the handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
and the meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest
and the meal offering of libations, and the bird burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הַמֶּלַח נְתוּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 6 by proving that salt was given for hides.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהנים were given salt for curing hides of קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the three places salt was kept, including the לשכת המלח for hides

steps.title: A new reading of שמואל: salt for eating קדשים is allowed, salt for ordinary food is not
steps.stepSummary: Because the first reading was disproven, the גמרא reinterprets שמואל. 'For their קרבנות' means for eating the קדשים they receive. 'Not for eating' means not for eating חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'for their offerings' mean? For eating their offerings. And what does 'for eating' mean? Eating ordinary, non-holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: The first explanation of שמואל fell apart, so the גמרא gives a new explanation of his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, 'eating' meant salting קדשים meat, and the קשיא showed that refusing salt for this made no sense. Now salting קדשים meat falls under the allowed category, 'their קרבנות'. The forbidden category, 'eating', is moved to ordinary food (חולין).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping the earlier explanation for a new one
Eating their offerings: the כהנים eating their share of קדשים
Ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'for their offerings' mean?
For eating their offerings,
and what does 'for eating' mean?
Eating of ordinary food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading of step 5 that was knocked down in steps 6-7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Eating' meant salting קדשים meat, which made no sense to forbid
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Their קרבנות' covers eating קדשים; only salt for ordinary food is forbidden

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that ordinary food gets no מקדש salt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that there is no need to say this. Ordinary food has no place in the מקדש anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ordinary food? That's obvious! What would it be doing there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. Why would שמואל need to teach something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that חולין food is not normally found in the עזרה. If so, nobody would think of salting it with the מקדש's salt, and שמואל's statement would teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
What are they doing there? (Why would it be in that place at all?)

phrases.english: Ordinary food? That's obvious!
What would it be doing there?
phrases.notes: 'There' means inside the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The new reading that 'eating' means eating חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חולין doesn't belong in the עזרה, so forbidding the salt for it is pointless to say

steps.title: כהנים do eat ordinary food with a מנחה, yet still get no salt for it
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים are taught to eat חולין and תרומה along with the leftover מנחה so they eat it while full. So חולין is in the עזרה, and even so the מקדש's salt may not be used on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the Master said: 'They shall eat' teaches that they should eat ordinary food and תרומה along with it, so that it is eaten in a state of fullness, even so, we do not give them the holy salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that ordinary food really is eaten in the עזרה, so שמואל's ruling is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא learns from the word 'יאכלו' that the כהנים eat other food together with the leftover מנחה, so they eat the holy food while already full. Since חולין is there, one might think the holy salt may be used on it too. שמואל teaches that it may not.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to כהנים
While satisfied, eating holy food when already full
Holy salt belonging to the מקדש

phrases.english: Even though the Master said: 'They shall eat'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:9. The פסוק is about the leftover מנחה that אהרן and his sons eat.

phrases.english: teaches that they should eat ordinary food and terumah along with it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the leftover מנחה.

phrases.english: so that it is eaten in a state of fullness,
even so,
we do not give them the holy salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is real and not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חולין is never in the עזרה, so the ruling is pointless
steps.terutzMaskana: חולין is eaten there with the מנחה, so it is a real case, and the salt is still not given
steps.whatToRemember: On this second reading of שמואל, כהנים may use the מקדש's salt for the קדשים they eat, but not for the ordinary food they eat alongside it. רבינא supports this reading in step 11, and רב מרדכי pushes back in step 17.

steps.title: רבינא shows the new reading is more logical
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי that the new reading makes sense. The old reading ('salting their own קרבנות') would mean the כהנים needed a special בית דין rule just to get salt that regular ישראלים already get.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: So too it is logical. For if you think 'for their offerings' means to salt them, then the reason is only that the court made a condition, but without the court's condition, no? Now, if we give salt to Israelites, would we not give it to כהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a logical support for the second reading by showing a problem with the first reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה presents the salt as a special rule of בית דין. If that rule were just about salting the כהנים' own offerings, it would mean that without it they get nothing. But ישראלים get salt for their offerings with no special rule, so the כהנים surely do too. So the בית דין rule must be about something extra: salt for eating קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical; introduces support for a position
It enters your mind; 'if you were to think'
The court made a condition (a special enactment)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the בית דין rule had to grant something beyond what every ישראל already receives.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
So too it is logical,
for if you think
that 'for their offerings' means to salt them,
then the reason is only that the court made a condition,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא אַתְנִי בֵּית דִּין – לָא?
phrases.english: so without the court's condition, no?
Now, if we give salt to Israelites,
would we not give it to כהנים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of steps 8-10 by showing a flaw in the reading of step 5
steps.raayaObject: The second reading of שמואל (salt for eating קדשים)
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: ישראלים already get salt for their offerings, so a בית דין rule can't be needed for כהנים to salt theirs

steps.title: A ברייתא begins: maybe one must bring salt for a מנחה from home
steps.stepSummary: To prove that ישראלים get salt for their offerings, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It opens with a 'might think' argument: salt should come from home, just like לבונה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One might think that someone who says 'I take upon myself a meal offering' must bring salt from his home, just as he brings frankincense from his home. And it is logical: it says 'bring a meal offering' and 'bring salt,' and it says 'bring a meal offering' and 'bring frankincense.' Just as frankincense comes from his home, so too salt comes from his home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבינא's claim that ישראלים are given salt. This part is only the setup, the 'one might think' idea, and the ברייתא's real conclusion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares salt to לבונה, since both are brought together with a מנחה. Because a person brings his own לבונה, one might think he must bring his own salt too. The ברייתא raises this idea only to reject it afterward and show that salt is supplied by the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think; introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject
I take upon myself a מנחה; a vow to bring a meal offering
Frankincense placed on a מנחה
And it is logical; introduces a reasoned argument

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking salt must come from home! This is only the 'might think' part of the ברייתא. Its conclusion, coming next, is the opposite.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One might think that someone who says
'I take upon myself a meal offering'
must bring salt from his home,
just as he brings frankincense from his home?
And it is logical:
It says 'bring a meal offering' and 'bring salt,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13.

phrases.english: and it says 'bring a meal offering' and 'bring frankincense.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1-2.

phrases.english: Just as frankincense comes from his home,
so too salt comes from his home.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source for step 11's claim that ישראלים are given salt
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that ישראלים receive the מקדש's salt for their offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about salt for a vowed מנחה (its conclusion continues after this)

steps.title: Maybe salt is like wood, which comes from the public
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises another option. Salt and wood are both 'brought' with a מנחה, and wood comes from communal supplies. So salt should be communal too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: the Torah says to bring a מנחה and bring salt, and it says to bring a מנחה and bring wood. Just as wood comes from communal supplies, salt should also come from communal supplies!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own first idea (that salt comes from home, like לבונה). It suggests comparing salt to wood instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 the ברייתא compared salt to לבונה, which the owner brings from home. Here it points out that salt can also be compared to wood, since a מנחה needs both. Wood comes from communal supplies, so this comparison leads to the opposite result.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way. The ברייתא uses this phrase to introduce a competing line of reasoning.
Wood, used to burn the offerings on the מזבח
From the public's property, meaning communal supplies paid for by everyone

phrases.english: Or perhaps, go this way:
It is stated: bring a meal offering and bring salt,
and it is stated: bring a meal offering and bring wood —
phrases.notes: This isn't an exact quote. A מנחה can't be burned on the מזבח without wood, so wood has to come along with it.

phrases.english: just as wood is from communal supplies,
so too salt should be from communal supplies!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing comparison against the לבונה comparison from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'might think' comparison of salt to לבונה (salt comes from home)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt can just as easily be compared to wood, which is communal, so the comparison to לבונה is not compelling.

steps.title: Wood is the better match because it applies to all offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא weighs the two comparisons. Salt and wood are both used with every type of offering, while לבונה is not. So the wood comparison looks stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one salt is more like. We learn something used with all offerings from something else used with all offerings. Don't let לבונה prove otherwise, since it is not used with all offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to decide between the two comparisons. It argues that salt is more like wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt goes on every קרבן, and wood is needed for every קרבן. לבונה only goes with מנחות. Since salt and wood share this wide reach, salt should follow wood and come from communal supplies.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which one it resembles, a way of weighing two comparisons
We learn or derive one law from another
That applies to all the offerings

phrases.english: Let us see to which it is similar:
We derive a matter that applies to all offerings
phrases.notes: He means salt.

phrases.english: from a matter that applies to all offerings,
phrases.notes: He means wood.

phrases.english: and do not let frankincense prove otherwise,
since it does not apply to all offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the wood comparison from Step 13 over the לבונה comparison from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That salt should be compared to wood and so come from communal supplies
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature that salt and wood are used with every offering, while לבונה is not

steps.title: No, salt is like לבונה because they share one vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back. Salt and לבונה both go into the same vessel as the מנחה, while wood does not. So maybe salt should follow לבונה after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: we learn something that comes with the מנחה in one vessel from something else that comes with it in one vessel. Don't let wood prove otherwise, since it does not come with the מנחה in one vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא swings back and defends the לבונה comparison. It uses a different shared feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt and לבונה are physically placed with the מנחה in the same כלי, while wood is separate. That closeness is a good reason to compare salt to לבונה. Now the ברייתא is stuck: each comparison has a solid point, so logic alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: That comes along with it (with the מנחה)
In one vessel
Let them prove, meaning be used as a counter-example

steps.confusionAlert: Here the ברייתא is not reaching a conclusion. It shows that both comparisons are equally strong, which is why it will need a פסוק in the next step.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, go this way:

phrases.aramaic: דָּנִין דָּבָר הַבָּא עִמָּהּ בִּכְלִי אֶחָד,
phrases.english: We derive a matter that comes with it in one vessel,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מנחה, and the matter here is salt.

phrases.english: from a matter that comes with it in one vessel,
phrases.notes: He means לבונה.

phrases.english: and do not let wood prove otherwise,
since it does not come with it in one vessel!

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: דָּנִין דָּבָר הַבָּא עִמָּהּ בִּכְלִי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 14 and returns to the לבונה comparison from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument in Step 14 that salt is more like wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt shares a different, physical feature with לבונה (the same vessel), which wood lacks. So the wood comparison is not clearly better.

steps.title: A פסוק proves salt comes from communal supplies
steps.stepSummary: Since logic was deadlocked, the ברייתא brings a גזירה שוה. 'ברית עולם' is said about salt and about the לחם הפנים. The לחם הפנים is communal, so salt is communal too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'It is an everlasting covenant of salt.' And elsewhere it says: 'From the children of Israel, an everlasting covenant.' Just as there it is from communal supplies, here too it is from communal supplies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the back-and-forth with a פסוק. It concludes that salt comes from communal supplies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ברית עולם' appear about salt and about the לחם הפנים, which is a communal offering. Through this shared wording (a גזירה שוה), salt takes on the same rule: it comes from communal supplies. This proves that every ישראל gets salt for his offering for free, which is what רבינא needed in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches, used to bring a verse that settles the question
Covenant of salt
There, in another place in the Torah
Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same words in both places

steps.whatToRemember: Salt for קרבנות comes from communal supplies, learned from 'ברית עולם'. So ישראלים already get salt for free. רבינא argues that the כהנים would then not need a special בית דין rule for salting their offerings, so שמואל's rule must be about salt for eating קדשים. Step 17 answers this argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof for רבינא's point in Step 11, which supports the second reading of שמואל. Step 17 goes on to challenge that support.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'It is an everlasting covenant of salt,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:19

phrases.english: and there it says:
'From the children of Israel, an everlasting covenant,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:8, about the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: just as there it is from communal supplies,
so too here it is from communal supplies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the deadlock between Steps 13 to 15 with a פסוק, and completes the proof begun in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Salt for all offerings comes from communal supplies, based on the גזירה שוה of 'ברית עולם' with the לחם הפנים. This confirms that ישראלים get salt, which supports the reinterpretation of שמואל.

steps.title: The rule for כהנים is needed only according to בן בוכרי
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי reports that רב שישא בריה דרב אידי explained the משנה's rule letting כהנים use communal salt. It is needed only according to בן בוכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי told רב אשי: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says the משנה's rule is needed only according to בן בוכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי pushes back on רבינא's argument from step 11. He defends the first reading of שמואל, that the court let the כהנים salt their own offerings, by saying the court's rule is needed only according to בן בוכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא argued that ישראלים get salt for free, so the כהנים would need no court rule to salt their offerings. רב מרדכי answers that communal salt is bought with everyone's half-shekel. According to בן בוכרי, כהנים do not have to give the half-shekel, so they might seem to have no share in it. That is why a court rule was needed, and the first reading of שמואל can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for… (this rule only matters in a specific case)
A תנא who holds that כהנים are not obligated in the half-shekel

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: This is what Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi says:
It is needed only according to ben Bukhri.
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה's rule that the court let כהנים use the communal salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's argument (steps 11-16) by limiting the משנה's rule to בן בוכרי. This revives the first reading of שמואל from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to one view (בן בוכרי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since salt is communal, the משנה's rule for כהנים seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule matters only for בן בוכרי, who exempts כהנים from the half-shekel. So the first reading of שמואל (salting their own offerings) can stand after all.

steps.title: בן בוכרי and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי argue about כהנים and the shekel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. בן בוכרי says a כהן who gives the shekel is not sinning, which implies he does not have to give it. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says a כהן who does not give it is sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said that בן בוכרי testified in יבנה that a כהן who gives the shekel is not a sinner. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: No, a כהן who does not give it is a sinner. The כהנים just read a פסוק in a way that suits themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for בן בוכרי's opinion, so we can see what he holds about כהנים and the half-shekel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בוכרי's words "is not a sinner" only make sense if the כהן was not obligated to begin with. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says the opposite: כהנים are obligated like everyone else. He says the ones who don't pay are relying on their own reading of a פסוק, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives the half-shekel coin
A sinner
Testified (passed on a tradition)
Interpret for their own benefit

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
Rabbi Yehuda said,
ben Bukhri testified in Yavne:
Any כהן who gives the shekel is not a sinner.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to him:
Not so;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל חוֹטֵא,
phrases.english: rather, any כהן who does not give the shekel is a sinner,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים דּוֹרְשִׁין מִקְרָא זֶה לְעַצְמָן:
phrases.english: but the כהנים interpret this verse to their own advantage:

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֵעִיד בֶּן בּוּכְרִי בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows where בן בוכרי's opinion, mentioned in step 17, comes from.
steps.raayaObject: That בן בוכרי holds כהנים are not obligated in the shekel
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שקלים, the testimony in Yavne

steps.title: The כהנים' reason for not paying the shekel
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים quote the פסוק that a כהן's מנחה must be fully burned. If they paid, the communal מנחות would partly belong to them, and then those מנחות could not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Every meal offering of a כהן shall be entirely burned; it shall not be eaten." If the עומר, the שתי הלחם, and the לחם הפנים belong partly to us, how could they be eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and spells out the פסוק the כהנים use to excuse themselves from the shekel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה owned by a כהן must be burned completely. The עומר, שתי הלחם, and לחם הפנים are bought with shekel money and are normally eaten. So the כהנים argue that if they had a share in them, those offerings would become a כהן's מנחה and could not be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה brought by a כהן, which is burned completely
Entirely (burned completely)
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

phrases.english: "And every meal offering of a כהן shall be entirely burned;
it shall not be eaten"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְעוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
phrases.english: Since the עומר, the two loaves, and the shewbread
would be ours,
phrases.notes: These offerings are bought with shekel money. If the כהנים paid, they would own a share.

phrases.english: how could they be eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה by giving the פסוק the כהנים rely on.
steps.raayaObject: The reasoning behind exempting כהנים from the shekel

steps.title: According to בן בוכרי, a כהן who pays should be sinning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בן בוכרי. If a כהן does not have to give the shekel, then giving it would mean bringing his own private, non-holy money into the communal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בן בוכרי: since he isn't obligated to bring it at all, when he does bring it he should also be a sinner, because he brings חולין into the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בן בוכרי can say a כהן who pays is "not a sinner," when it looks like he is doing something wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings must be paid for by the community. A coin the כהן did not owe seems to be his private money. Using it for communal offerings would be like bringing non-holy, private property into the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; in the first place
Non-holy items brought into the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
Brings in

phrases.english: And according to ben Bukhri,
since from the start he is not obligated to bring it,
when he does bring it, he is also a sinner,
since he brings non-sacred items into the Temple courtyard.
phrases.notes: His coin counts as his own private money, not the community's, so the offerings bought with it look like his private property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבֶן בּוּכְרִי, כֵּיוָן דִּלְכַתְּחִילָּה לָא מִיחַיַּיב לְאֵיתוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions בן בוכרי's statement, quoted in step 18, that a כהן who pays is not a sinner.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן בוכרי's claim that a כהן who gives the shekel is not a sinner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unobligated payment is private money, so using it for communal offerings brings חולין into the עזרה.

steps.title: The כהן hands his shekel over to the community
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כהן brings his coin and gives it over fully to the community. So it becomes communal money and is not private.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings it and hands it over to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The כהן gives up ownership of his coin to the community, so it counts as communal money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the coin is handed over to the ציבור, it is no longer his private property. Offerings bought with it are truly communal, so nothing private is being brought into the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Handed over (gave ownership)
The community

steps.whatToRemember: According to בן בוכרי, כהנים don't have to give the shekel. That is why the משנה needed a court rule letting them use communal salt. A כהן who chooses to pay is fine, because he hands his coin over to the community.

phrases.english: He brings it and hands it over to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the coin becomes communal property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unobligated coin stays the כהן's private money.
steps.terutzMaskana: He transfers it to the ציבור, so it is communal money.

steps.title: Opening the 'you might have thought' explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why the salt rule is needed for בן בוכרי. It opens with the phrase 'it might enter your mind to say.' The actual mistaken idea comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to tell us the wrong idea we might have had according to בן בוכרי, which the salt rule comes to correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the salt rule is needed only according to בן בוכרי, but did not yet say why. The phrase סלקא דעתך אמינא introduces a הוה אמינא: a reasonable but mistaken first thought. Once we hear that thought, we will see why the salt rule had to be taught.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind; you might have thought
I would say; introduces the mistaken first thought

steps.confusionAlert: This phrase is not the conclusion. It introduces an idea the גמרא is about to reject, so do not treat what follows as the final הלכה.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to Step 17's claim that the salt rule is needed only according to בן בוכרי. It starts to explain that need, now that Steps 18-21 have laid out בן בוכרי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting up a הוה אמינא (a mistaken first thought) to show why the rule is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not yet stated. The next line will give the mistaken thought according to בן בוכרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. The salt rule will turn out to be needed to correct this mistaken thought.
